title: Timber floor restoration: scope, boundaries and what this training does not grant
audience: New and existing timber floor restoration workers, and the supervisors who accept and approve their jobs.
learningOutcomes: Describe the timber floor restoration work that is included in and excluded from the approved scope.
Identify when a job falls outside the scope and must be referred instead of performed.
Explain why completing this lesson does not grant a licence or authority to do regulated work.
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: SafeWork SA, Asbestos licences: Class A, Class B and assessor licence (no date shown); Safe Work Australia, Model WHS laws: which jurisdictions have adopted them (no date shown).

instruction.heading: What timber floor restoration includes
instruction.body: Timber floor restoration brings an existing timber floor back to a clean, serviceable and finished condition. Within an approved scope this can include sanding and screening, filling small surface defects in boards, staining, oiling or sealing, recoating, and cleaning up the dust and residue the work creates. The job is defined by a written scope that names the rooms, the finish to be applied, the surfaces excluded and the outcome the client has agreed. A worker does not widen that scope on their own judgement, even when the extra work looks easy.

instruction.heading: What the course excludes
instruction.body: Structural timber repair, subfloor and joist work, and any decision that a floor is structurally sound are outside this course and usually outside the job. Installing a new floor belongs to the flooring trade, and floating floors sit in the tiling business. Routine care of sealed timber is covered in the hard floor care course. Work on a floor that may contain lead paint, asbestos adhesive or asbestos-backed vinyl is excluded until a documented assessment has set the controls. In South Australia, SafeWork SA's asbestos licence page (page date not shown) says that removing asbestos-backed vinyl needs a Class A licence.

instruction.heading: Training is not a licence
instruction.body: Completing this course, or any Skilled lesson, does not give a licence, certificate or authority to do regulated work. Whether a licence, registration or notification is needed depends on the state or territory, the material and the activity. Where a licence is required, the work goes to a person who holds that licence.

instruction.heading: Why scope is checked before the first machine starts
instruction.body: A sanding job changes the floor quickly. Once a board is cut through, a finish has been stripped, or old material has been disturbed, the damage or the exposure cannot simply be undone. The scope and the site conditions are therefore checked before any machine starts, and any change is agreed in writing before work continues. The scope record protects the worker, the client and the business, and it is the first document an assessor will ask for.

procedure: Read the written scope and confirm the rooms, the finish and the excluded items.
Check the site against the scope, including the floor type, the age of the building and any signs of older materials.
Stop and refer any item outside the approved scope, and record the referral.
Confirm the licence and notification position for the state or territory before accepting work that may need one.
Do not start regulated or uncertain work on the assumption that it is allowed.
Record the scope confirmation and any variation before starting.

workedExamples.situation: A homeowner asks you to sand the whole house, fix a bouncy patch by the kitchen where the floor sags, and remove old carpet glue from the hallway. The building looks about 60 years old.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which parts can be accepted, which must be referred, and what must happen before any machine is used?
workedExamples.reasoning: The sag suggests a possible subfloor or joist problem. That is structural and outside the scope, so refer it to a qualified builder and do not promise a fix. Removing old glue in a building of this age may disturb adhesive that contains asbestos, so the hallway glue must not be scraped, cut or sanded until it has been assessed. Sanding sound boards can be quoted only after the assessment and its controls are in place. Record the referral and the variation, and get written agreement before work starts.

equipmentAndPpe: Client and property details, including access instructions
Form or tablet for the scope record and variation request

commonErrors.error: Taking on structural or subfloor work because the client describes the floor as 'a bit fixed'.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer structural and subfloor concerns to a qualified person and record the referral.

commonErrors.error: Assuming the course or a card allows any sanding job.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the licence and notification position for the state or territory and the material before accepting.

commonErrors.error: Starting work before the scope has been confirmed.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the scope and every variation in writing before the first machine starts.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson does not grant a licence, certificate or authority. Completing it is not evidence that the holder may carry out any licensed or regulated work.

Asbestos removal is licensed in some jurisdictions. In South Australia, SafeWork SA's licence page (page date not shown) describes a Class A licence for friable and non-friable asbestos, including asbestos-backed vinyl, and a Class B licence for non-friable material such as floor tiles, which the page's overview limits to removal of more than 10 square metres. Licensing body: SafeWork SA.
Check the position for each jurisdiction before accepting work.

Victoria is the only jurisdiction that has not implemented the model WHS laws, so Victorian duties sit under its own legislation (Safe Work Australia, page date not shown). State differences must be checked for every job.

qualityStandard: The scope is recorded with included and excluded items before work starts.
Each item outside the scope is referred and recorded, not performed.
The licence and notification position for the job's state or territory is recorded.
documentationEvidence: Agreed scope showing included and excluded items
Referral record for any structural, lead or asbestos concern
summary: Work only to the written, confirmed scope.
Structural, subfloor and unassessed hazardous material is referred, not repaired.
Training does not grant a licence. Check the position for each state and territory.
referencesAtEnd: Official sources to recheck before any job: SafeWork SA, Asbestos licences: Class A, Class B and assessor licence (no date shown); Safe Work Australia, Model WHS laws: which jurisdictions have adopted them (no date shown).

knowledgeChecks.question: Which item is outside the approved scope of timber floor restoration?
options: Repairing a sagging floor that may be caused by the joists
Sanding and screening a sound timber floor in the house
Applying an approved finish after sanding the floor boards

knowledgeChecks.question: Does completing this course give a licence to do regulated work?
options: Yes, once the course is finished and the certificate is printed
No. It is training only and does not grant a licence or authority
Yes, if the client agrees to it in writing on the day

knowledgeChecks.question: The client's scope is unclear. What should you do?
options: Start the cheapest part and decide the rest later on the job site
Use your own judgement and do not record it in the file at all
Confirm the scope in writing before starting, and refer any item outside it

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the purpose of a written variation?
options: It is only needed for invoicing the client at the end of the job
It replaces the hazard assessment that the site requires for the job
It is a formality after the work is done and the floor is finished
It records approval for any change to the agreed scope before work continues

knowledgeChecks.question: Which finding is the best reason to stop work and refer?
options: A small gap between two boards in the floor near the wall and door
Material that may contain asbestos has been found and has not been assessed
The client is not at home during the visit and the whole job
